confidentiality: Confidential - for Audit Committee use only
executive_summary: Internal Audit reviewed the procurement-to-payment process across three business units. Controls over vendor onboarding and payment approval are generally in place, but weaknesses in purchase order approval and contract monitoring expose the company to unauthorised spending and overpayment risk.
key_highlights: 12% of purchase orders were approved after the invoice date
3 active vendors had no valid contract on file
Segregation of duties conflicts found in 2 user roles
Payment approval controls operated effectively for all samples tested
audit_scope: Vendor onboarding, purchase requisition and PO approval, contract management, invoice matching and payment processing for Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand units.

findings.title: Purchase orders raised after goods or services were received
findings.recommendation: Enforce system block on invoices without an approved PO; report exceptions monthly

findings.title: Expired vendor contracts still in active use
findings.recommendation: Set up contract expiry alerts 90 days ahead and review the active vendor list quarterly

findings.title: Users able to both create vendors and approve payments
findings.recommendation: Remove conflicting access and run a quarterly user access review

findings.title: Three-way match tolerance set higher than policy
findings.recommendation: Align system tolerance to the 2% limit in the procurement policy

conclusion: Management has agreed to all recommendations. Internal Audit will follow up on the two high-risk findings in Q1 2027.
